All it took was a "Pavel" to ruin our fondness of your restaurant
Oct 2026 • Family
Dear Refinery,
You held a special place for me and my husband. We always loved the atmosphere, food and service. Don't get me wrong, you food is still good and your staff are sweet and professional as always. Saturday night made me look at your restaurant in a different light. My family (me, husband, daughter and baby) came to your restaurant for dinner. We hadn't made a reservation. A vietnamese staff at the entrance was trying to see if we can be accommodated. The assistant manager Pavel told us they were full. So we went next door for dinner. After dinner we were craving dessert especially your crepe suzette flambed. We thought we would check if there was availability at your restaurant. When we got there, the staff at the entrance said we could sit at the bar. Once inside, staff told us that a table would be free soon and we would be moved from the bar area to the main dining area. For some reason that didnt sit well with your manager. Suddenly we saw your assistant manager Pavel turn up and looked obviously upset about it and was lecturing the staff. It looked like a big issue because there was alot of talks being given to the staff inside the restaurant and then they were given a talk outside the restaurant. After that the staff kept apologizing to us and feeling really bad about not being able to seat us at the regualr tables. We were ok with that. Pavel had no deceny to approach us to sort anything out.
In fact he earlier told us that a child seat was not available while it was clearly unused in a corner. 

 We started to feel very uncomfortable like we were not welcomed there at all by him. I even told one of your staff, if it's an issue we are here, then we will leave beacuse of all the bickering we saw. Pavel went out of his way to ensure we were not welcomed at your restaurant. 

The amount of times he was cribbing at the staff who had accomodated us and passing comments like "i'm an idiot" to them. We wanted to leave. But after all the trouble and crap the staff were getting, we stayed but changed the order to something we could get quicker. Mind you we were full aware of walk-ins that were happily being accomodated. When waiting to pay the bill, Pavel happened to pass by and my husband was handing him the bill folder. He just walked by snatched it without stopping or acknowledging us. We felt sick in our stomach. 

The no.of times your other staff apologised, including those who knew us from before, was really sad. Your assistant managers behaviour was very unprofessional, appears he lacks experience in this industry and bordered on immature. An individual like him will ruin the reputation of a Saigon institution.

Written October 26, 2026

Fantastic French Food in a Unique Historical Setting
Feb 2025 • Couples
We stumbled upon The Refinery while looking for a late lunch, and everything about the meal was fantastic!
The bread used for our sandwiches were made in-house, and perfectly reminiscent of what I’ve had in Paris. My favorite drink is a passion fruit martini, and they can be difficult to find. But it so happened that The Refinery’s specialty was in fact a passion fruit martini, and it did not disappoint! It was a perfect balance of sweet and refreshing.
We also enjoyed learning about the historical setting of the building, and they did a good job of leaning into it with tasteful decor accenting the story of the old opium refinery.
Finally, the pricing was extremely affordable by western standards. We had two entrees complete with sides, an alcoholic drink, and coffee and the total bill was $30 USD!
Overall, if you’re looking for a break from the hustle and bustle of the city, and enjoy history and classic French food, The Refinery is a must visit!

Wonderful vibes, beautifully plated and delicious French cuisine done well
Dec 2024 • Friends
Wonderful vibes because:
Yes, most talked about this restaurant being in the Opium factory from colonial times. But so are other restaurants within the same compound. What makes Refinery stand out was that they also made the entire place classy with both the well-stocked dusky-lit bar up front and also comfy cushioned leather seats in the romantically and comfortably darkened raw-bricks corners. Servers were friendly and happy to answer all our amateurish questions about the dishes.

Beautifully plated and delicious French dishes:
From our flambé appetizer shrimps, to comforting onion soup, to the generously fat and juicy foie gras, to the really beautifully plated duck confit, to finally what I think is their pièce de résistance (the again, I haven't tried their steaks and bouillabaisse) - Duck Magret with Orange Sauce, Roasted Vegetables & Rosemary Baby Potatoes... everything was done so well in terms of presentation, generous in quantity, and the duck magret was truly cooked perfectly to be both tenderly pink and flavorful.

French Brasserie In Saigon satisfies
Sep 2024 • Couples
This was my second time eating here in just under a year (i have been overseas for work).

The food is definitely French Brasserie style and the chef does it very well. We started off with a delicious Pâté de Champagne and a melt in your mouth Whole Baked Camembert with walnuts and honey. With these we just had a Blanc de Blanc Champagne. For our main we both decided on a serving of Angus Beef Fillet Mignon for two and we paired this with a lovely Loire Valley Cabernet Franc. Everything was tasty.

The only thing missing for me was that the staff seem to have changed a lot from the last time i ate there. In particular I remember a European gentleman who was super knowledgeable about wine and gave a lot of great advice and fun anecdotes. He had actually made my first visit so memorable that I was determined to come back this visit to Saigon. When I asked after him, the staff member just looked at me blankly. I guess it is normal, people move on. Anyway the food is the main reason we go somewhere and that was spot on.

Dear Sir,

I actually remember you clearly. You were sitting at table N22 (which is actually 2 tables pushed together to create a 4) in our non-smoking section.
I would like to point out that The Refinery is a BISTRO and that in traditional bistro fashion, table tops are small and usually arranged very close to each other. What I mean is that for a romantic dinner or if you wish to have a private conversation, a bistro is not the place to be. Bistros tend to be crowded and noisy and the neighbours' conversation can clearly be overheard. If you have been to France you know what I mean. There, the space between tables in no more than 6 inches and bistro owners never allow customers to use more tables than the number in their party requires. We have taught our staff according to these basics.

Regarding the meat, it was underdone indeed and I actually got it cooked to a medium for you. I apologised and I apologise again for the mistake. I suppose that the kitchen reheated your vegetables so that they wouldn't be cold the second time around and that they automatically added butter and salt (out of habit) which meant your veggies came out as too buttery and a little too salty. I offered something at the end of your meal so that you wouldn't leave our establishment with too bad an impression (especially because I knew you were a return customer). The owner was more than apologetic but I think the poor management of the situation by service staff left a bad taste in our mouths more so than the badly cooked food.

Whether I have eaten there in the bustling ambience of the lunch hour or at the more chilled dinner sitting in the evening, it feels like a piece of France in a Vietnamese context. It would be extremely easy to walk right past this great cluster of alfresco restaurants, in a leafy cul de sac courtyard, directly across Hai Ba Trung road next to the Park Hyatt Hotel, on the corner of Lam Son Square. Head under the archway toward the twinkling lights in back, and you will find a number of great restaurants with lively garden bars, lots of trees adorned with twinkling lights and cane furniture, and airconditioned renovated colonial restaurant interiors behind them.
The complex is a renovated olonial opium refinery (hence the name), with the main restaurant aptly called The Refinery. There is als the Hoa Tuc (meaning "opium poppy"), which runs Vietnamese cooking classes and a good upstairs bar/lounge/terrace. The refinery serves delicous contemporary French/Italian food, with good portion sizes at excellent prices, but the thing that really stands out is the speed at which the meals come out of the kitchen - there are many restaurants around the world that could take a leaf out of The Refinery's book!
